title: Robust Static Candidate-Branch Obstructions and Reduced Pole-Correction Bounds in a Chiral Operator-Spectral Framework
content: We analyze a specified finite-dimensional chiral operator-spectral candidate whose conservative sector consists of one positive spectral scale and four Hermitian family quadratic forms relative to a common family metric. We first prove that common positive rescaling preserves conservative mass ratios and static spectral subspaces, while simultaneous congruence of the family forms and metric preserves generalized spectra and metric-normalized overlaps. For the evaluated candidate, an analytic neighborhood criterion and its reproducible numerical realization show that every tuple within spectral-norm radius 2.5 × 10−2 of the four canonical family operators remains outside enlarged charged-lepton, CKM, PMNS reactor-entry, and electron-anchored tritium-endpoint acceptance regions. At this radius the muon-to-electron ratio is below 1.864, the best-permuted CKM distance exceeds 0.248, every admissible static electron-row neutrino overlap exceeds 0.245, and the lightest neutrino rest energy exceeds twelve tritium endpoints after electron anchoring. We then derive relabeling-independent lower bounds on the total reduced pole correction in a fixed conservative/counterterm decomposition. For passive self-adjoint open complements, the reduced kernel is operator-valued anti-Herglotz and the subthreshold pencil is strictly Loewner monotone; under the stated passive hypotheses this yields existence, uniqueness, positive residue, and Lipschitz stability of isolated real pole branches. The finite-dimensional scale and family data define the conservative candidate tested here, while the resulting theorems separate its invariant static limitations from the analytic requirements of a dynamical completion.
